cohort: The study included women who delivered at 40 weeks gestational age and beyond with uncomplicated pregnancies at a tertiary care hospital.
finding: Increasing gestational age beyond 40 weeks is associated with an increased rate of LSCS, fetal distress, intrauterine fetal death, birth asphyxia, NICU admissions, and maternal morbidities like post-partum hemorrhage, perineal tears, and gaped episiotomy.
mod_finding: The percentage of Lower Segment Caesarian Section (LSCS) was found to increase as gestational age increases, with fetal distress being the most common indication.
